verdict.rationale: Zapier documents that it stores app connections centrally and handles credentials for users. MCP marketing mentions "managed connections" and "permissions you control", and teammates can get view or edit access to an MCP server on Team and Enterprise plans. None of this documents sharing a specific credential with teammates or granting per-credential usage permissions. Missing for 10: documented sharing of app connections or credentials with a team, per-credential access controls defining who can use which connection, detail beyond marketing-level mentions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can store connection credentials centrally, share them with my team, and control who can use which credential

citations.quote: Zapier brings in your existing app connections automatically. Gmail, Slack, Salesforce, whatever you've already set up in Zapier is ready to go.
Zapier handles OAuth, credentials, and API complexity so you never touch a token.
Account-level restrictions, managed connections, and workspace controls apply to all of them.
all with managed auth and permissions you control
Give teammates view or edit access to your MCP server on Team and Enterprise plans.
